standard_prerequisites.name: Infinitary formulas and back-and-forth relations
standard_prerequisites.statement: The complexity classes Pi^in_alpha and Sigma^in_alpha of L_{omega_1,omega} formulas, the back-and-forth relation =_alpha, and Scott rank as the least ordinal whose Sigma^in formulas define all tuple orbits; all three ranks are defined in the retained context excerpt.

standard_prerequisites.name: Labeled trees and the tree-of-tuples construction
standard_prerequisites.statement: The vocabulary of labeled trees, the finite atomic diagram coding used as a label, and the replication of every branch; the article's own translation lemma (source lines 234-286) is delivered with its complete proof and is not assumed.

core_obligations: Push forward an arbitrary Pi^in_alpha formula about a tuple of the structure to a Pi^in_alpha tree formula holding exactly at the nodes above the tuple's code, by induction on the complexity of the formula (source lines 250-264).

Pull a Pi^in_alpha tree formula back to a Pi^in_alpha formula of the structure along the Turing-computable parameterized tree-of-tuples embedding, using that the image contains the parameterized tree of the given structure (source lines 266-285).

Derive both rank inequalities: define the orbit of a tuple of the structure by the pulled-back formula, and conversely describe the orbit of a tuple of the tree by a Sigma^in_1 description of its finite subtree together with the pushed-forward orbit formulas of its leaves, using the infinite replication of branches to extend the resulting isomorphisms to an automorphism (source lines 313-331).

proof_roadmap.step: Statement and complete proof of the article's own translation lemma, delivered as local support.
The immediately following author proof of thm:treeofstructuressr.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the rank identity SR(A) = SR(T_A) for the replicated tree of tuples T_A (statement, source lines 309-311). Its work is the two-directional translation of Pi^in_alpha formulas (source lines 234-286) together with the orbit reconstruction at 312-332: an orbit in T_A must be described by a finite subtree plus the orbit formulas of its leaves, and the infinite replication of branches is what turns the resulting subtree isomorphism into an automorphism. A routine induction on tuples does not give this, because the class of trees of tuples is not definable inside the labeled trees and the pullback direction needs the parameterized embedding; the article says so explicitly at 287-293.
